speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing that history. To better understand the nature of your tremors and memory issues, can you tell me if your hand movements are shaking at rest or only when you are trying to use your hands? Additionally, have you or anyone noticed any changes in your speech or balance recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old man accompanied by his wife. The patient first noticed the tremor in his left hand 1 year ago, which has been progressively worsening. Recently, he has faced difficulty in performing tasks that require steadiness, such as reading. His wife has observed a decline in his memory, taking note of his forgetfulness in paying bills, a task she has since had to assume.

speaker: Doctor
text: Is the tremor in your left hand more pronounced when your arm is relaxed at your side, or does it appear only when you are holding a cup or writing? Also, has your wife noticed any changes in your personality, judgment, or gait stability?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Resting tremor worse on the left hand. I also have Soft speech, Reduced facial expressions, Memory decline, Difficulty in managing finances.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Parkinson's Disease. The combination of a unilateral resting tremor, soft speech (hypophonia), reduced facial expressions (masked facies), and executive dysfunction (memory decline/finances) is highly characteristic of Parkinson's disease, likely in the mild-to-moderate stage. REQUEST IMAGES: Head MRI to rule out other causes like vascular parkinsonism.
